current_disclosures.section: Overview > Our Business > Foundry > Process Technology
current_disclosures.summary: Intel 7 (HVM 2017) continues in production for 13th/14th Gen Core processors and was utilized for the majority of internal production by revenue in 2025, expected to remain nearly half in 2026. Intel 4 (HVM 2023) uses EUV lithography, was utilized for Intel Core Ultra Series 1, and represented a modest portion of 2025 production with decreasing expected contribution in 2026. Intel 3 (HVM 2024) is a derivative of Intel 4 used for Intel Xeon 6 Scalable processors, also representing a modest portion of 2025 production with increasing expected contribution in 2026.

materiality_analysis.reason: The 2025 disclosure significantly expands on production volume metrics by quantifying Intel 7 as 'majority... by revenue' with a specific forecast of 'almost half' for 2026, whereas 2024 only stated 'significant majority'. Crucially, it downgrades Intel 4's status from 'increasing portion' (2024) to 'modest portion' with a 'decreasing expected contribution' (2025), and updates Intel 3 from HVM in Oregon to a derivative of Intel 4 with 'modest' contribution. These are material shifts in the relative weight and trajectory of key manufacturing nodes.

comparisons.peer_topic: DRAM production nodes and future expectations
comparisons.peer_summary: The company shipped its industry's first 1β production node in 2023, produced majority 2024 bits on 1α and 1β nodes, and expects volume shipments of the 1γ node using EUV lithography in 2025.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron disclose the specific status and timeline of their next-generation manufacturing nodes utilizing EUV lithography. Intel describes Intel 3 (its second EUV node) being in high-volume manufacturing in 2024 and shifting to Ireland for 2025, while Micron states it expects volume shipments of its 1γ node, which employs EUV lithography, in 2025. Both highlight EUV adoption as a key step in their process roadmap, though they reference different node naming conventions (Intel 3 vs. 1γ) and specific production timelines.

sentences.text: ▪Intel 3, our second EUV lithography node, delivers further logic scaling and up to 18% performance-per-watt improvement over Intel 4. Intel 3 is offered to external foundry customers and is optimized for the needs of data center products. This node, which is produced in the same facilities as Intel 4, was in high-volume manufacturing in Oregon during 2024, with high-volume manufacturing shifted to Ireland for 2025. Intel's Xeon 6 Scalable server processor offerings are built on this technology.
We expect volume shipments in 2025 of our next generation of DRAM, the 1γ (1-gamma) node, which will employ EUV lithography production.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company is on track for volume production of 1-gamma DRAM using EUV lithography in calendar 2025 and has begun volume production of its Micron G9 NAND node.
comparisons.comparison: Micron confirms that its pilot production for the 1-gamma DRAM node using EUV lithography is progressing well with volume production expected in calendar 2025. This parallels Intel's disclosure that its Intel 3 EUV node is in high-volume manufacturing in 2024 with a shift to Ireland for 2025, illustrating both companies' active deployment of EUV technology for next-generation product generations.

comparisons.peer_topic: Product energy efficiency and Green500 performance
comparisons.peer_summary: NVIDIA's GPU-accelerated computing is optimized for energy efficiency and performance per watt. The company powered 24 of the top 30 most energy-efficient systems on the Green500 list, including the top supercomputer.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies address performance and efficiency metrics for their advanced technologies. Intel explicitly quantifies an 'up to 18% performance-per-watt improvement' for its Intel 3 node over Intel 4. Similarly, NVIDIA highlights that its GPU-accelerated computing is optimized for 'performance per watt' and cites its dominance on the Green500 list as evidence of this energy efficiency, demonstrating a shared industry focus on optimizing performance per watt for next-gen hardware.

comparisons.peer_topic: Processor architecture and AI Engine capabilities
comparisons.peer_summary: Qualcomm utilizes System-on-Chip architecture with heterogeneous computing, including Oryon and Kryo CPUs and Adreno GPUs, to enable high-performance, low-power computing. The Qualcomm AI Engine features dedicated hardware and the Hexagon NPU for high-performance on-device AI inference, supported by the AI Stack and AI Hub to simplify developer integration.
comparisons.comparison: Qualcomm describes its Oryon CPU cores as being custom-designed to deliver 'a new level of performance and efficiency' for integration into Snapdragon products. This aligns with Intel's disclosure of Intel 3 delivering 'up to 18% performance-per-watt improvement,' as both companies highlight architectural improvements aimed at enhancing performance efficiency in their respective processor technologies.
